sample_unit: survey respondents (mental health professionals); plus 12 interviewed clinicians

links.outcome: Clinician use of general-purpose AI amid workplace governance and privacy concerns
links.effect: 43.5% (121/278) reported daily administrative/clinician-support AI use and 33.1% (92/278) daily client-facing use; interviewees reported privacy, data security concerns and uneven workplace governance.
links.quote: Participants also raised concerns about privacy, data security, accuracy, client acceptability, overreliance, loss of human judgment, and uneven workplace governance.

links.outcome: Clinician-reported insufficient training or support for AI tools
links.effect: Insufficient training or support and limited confidence in judging outputs were among commonly endorsed concerns; no specific percentages given in the abstract.
links.quote: Commonly endorsed concerns included privacy and security, accuracy, insufficient training or support, limited confidence in judging outputs, and a preference for human judgment.

screen.reason: Mixed-methods survey and interview study investigating how Australian mental health professionals use general-purpose AI tools in routine clinical and administrative practice, including governance and safety concerns.
